mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome—I'm glad you're here. Imagine a life shaped by unshakeable faith and genuine, selfless devotion. That's the story we're about to experience together: the remarkable journey of Amy Carmichael. Her footsteps lead us from the bustling streets of Ireland all the way to the vibrant heart of India, where compassion wasn’t just a feeling—it was something she put into action every single day. In A Chance to Die: The Life and Legacy of Amy Carmichael, Elisabeth Elliot invites us to walk alongside a woman who refused to look away from suffering. Instead, Amy chose to embrace those who were forgotten or hurting. Along the way, we’ll find ourselves wrestling with big questions—like what does it really mean to sacrifice? How do we find purpose, and what’s the true cost of loving others deeply? As we follow Amy's transformation—from a spirited young woman to a trailblazing missionary—the heart of her legacy begins to shine through. You'll get a glimpse into her daily life in India: rescuing children from unthinkable exploitation, building a close-knit community rooted in faith, and navigating all the highs and lows of serving others. Elisabeth Elliot captures not just Amy’s choices, but the lasting ripple effects one life can have when it’s poured out for others. Together, let's set out on this journey—one that explores meaning, resilience, and hope. There’s so much to discover about the power of conviction and the beauty of a life lived for something greater than ourselves.

Chapter 1: Early Years—Seeds of Faith and Restlessness
You know, childhood is really a string of small awakenings, isn’t it? Those moments when the world slowly comes into focus, and you start to feel little questions stirring in your heart.
Picture a quiet town tucked away in Northern Ireland. That’s where Amy grew up, surrounded by the gentle rhythms of family life, Sunday church, and endless stretches of green countryside. Her days were filled with the simple joys and disappointments of a Victorian childhood—her mother’s warm embrace, her father’s steady expectations, and the comfort of familiar routines.
But underneath all of that, something restless was starting to grow inside her.
In Amy’s home, faith wasn’t just a set of distant rules—it was alive. Her mother’s whispered prayers and her father’s quiet honesty left a lasting mark, shaping how she saw the world. Still, Amy couldn’t just accept things at face value. She was curious, always asking questions, always searching for something deeper. She wanted a purpose that could help her make sense of both the beauty and the pain she saw around her.
Sometimes, though, the gap between what people preached and what they actually lived was painfully obvious. There was one Sunday, for example, when Amy was leaving church. She noticed a poor woman, shivering in the cold, completely ignored by the well-dressed crowd streaming past. That moment stuck with her—a quiet nudge, reminding her that real faith should be more than just words. It should lead to action, to sacrifice, to truly seeing those who are invisible.
As Amy got older, that sense of calling only grew stronger. She wasn’t satisfied with the narrow path set out for girls in her day. While many dreamed of marriage and security, Amy’s heart was pulled toward stories of missionaries and reformers—people who gave up everything for something bigger than themselves. The idea of pouring out her life for others, of making faith real through service, began to take root.
Of course, her journey wasn’t simple. When her father’s business failed, Amy’s family faced some tough times. The security she’d always known disappeared, replaced by uncertainty and struggle. But even in those hard moments, Amy found herself leaning on God in new ways. She started to believe that even loss could have meaning.
During these years, Amy’s restlessness turned into resolve. She began reaching out to the poor right in her own city—gathering children from the slums for Sunday school, visiting the sick, giving away whatever little she had. Most people didn’t notice these quiet acts, but for Amy, they were the start of a lifelong journey. The seeds of faith, watered by hardship and compassion, were quietly growing.
Looking back, it’s easy to see how those early experiences shaped everything that came after. The young girl who once questioned the gap between belief and action would spend her life closing that gap, one loving act at a time. And that restless spirit? It became the driving force behind a legacy that would reach far beyond anything she could have imagined.

Chapter 2: Finding Purpose—The Call to Serve Beyond Home
You know, for a lot of us, the shift from youth into adulthood really feels like standing at a crossroads—wondering where we fit in, and what we’re meant to do in this big, complicated world.
Amy totally understood that feeling. Her story is one of searching, of shouldering heavy responsibilities, and of listening to a quiet, persistent tug on her heart—a sense that her life was meant for something more than just her own needs.
After her family’s financial troubles, Amy found herself caring for her younger siblings and supporting her widowed mother. The daily routine was exhausting. Some days, the weight of it all felt almost too much to bear. But even with so many demands pressing in, Amy’s heart stayed open. She kept wondering if there was something more she was meant to do.
That’s when Amy crossed paths with the “Shawlies.” These were young women working long hours in the mills and factories, their heads wrapped in simple shawls instead of the fancy hats everyone else wore. Society often ignored them, treating them as if they didn’t matter. But Amy saw something different. She noticed their deep longing for meaning, their hope for dignity—and she couldn’t look away.
Week after week, Amy gathered the Shawlies for Bible study and conversation. She didn’t just offer spiritual wisdom—she gave them genuine friendship and a place to belong. It wasn’t easy. Some nights, Amy dragged herself home, completely worn out, wondering if any of it really mattered.
But over time, she saw real change. Women who once felt invisible discovered hope and a sense of belonging. That’s powerful, isn’t it? Amy realized that true service means stepping into someone else’s world, carrying their burdens with them, and loving without expecting anything in return.
This experience didn’t just change the Shawlies—it changed Amy. She started to dream about serving beyond her own community. Stories of missionaries working across the world captured her imagination, and she began to pray for direction.
Leaving home, though, was no small thing. Amy struggled with fear and doubt, fully aware of what it would cost her and her family. People questioned her, warned her about all the dangers and sacrifices. But that call to serve—to give her life for something bigger than herself—just wouldn’t go away.
After a lot of soul-searching and prayer, Amy decided to pursue missionary work. Her first try, heading to Japan, ended in disappointment. Health issues forced her to return home much sooner than she’d hoped. It was a crushing blow, and for a while, Amy wondered if her dreams were over. But deep down, she sensed her journey wasn’t finished yet.
Then, a new door opened—a chance to serve in India, a place facing deep poverty and injustice, but also incredible spiritual hunger. The idea was intimidating, but Amy felt a quiet confidence. This was where she belonged. So, with only a few goodbyes and not much fanfare, she set out for a country she’d never seen, trusting that God, who’d led her this far, wouldn’t leave her now.
The move to India changed everything for Amy. It was a step into the unknown—a leap of faith that challenged her, shaped her, and deepened her understanding of what real service looks like. All those lessons she’d learned with the Shawlies—compassion, humility, and sticking with it even when it’s hard—they would become even more important in the years ahead.

Chapter 3: India—Embracing a New World and Its Challenges
Imagine stepping off a train in a place where every sight, every sound, and even the air itself feels entirely new. That's what happened when Amy arrived in India. She was instantly surrounded by vibrant colors, unfamiliar music drifting through the streets, and traditions that stretched back for centuries. The heat was heavy and constant, the language a mystery, and daily life moved to a rhythm she’d never known before.
For a lot of people, a change like that would’ve been overwhelming. But Amy? She chose to lean into it—not with judgment, but with curiosity and respect. She figured out pretty quickly that good intentions just weren’t enough. She noticed the people she hoped to serve watched outsiders with suspicion, especially those who seemed to act superior or distant.
So, Amy decided to do things differently. She set aside her own preferences and began to truly adapt. She traded her Western clothes for the simple dress worn by local women, took the time to learn the language, and tried to live each day just as her neighbors did. It wasn’t just about blending in—it was about showing genuine respect for the people around her.
And people noticed. While some missionaries kept their distance, sticking to their own customs, Amy’s humility and willingness to listen slowly earned her trust. She made it a point to listen more than she spoke, always trying to understand before offering advice. That’s when she realized—real change happens through relationships, built one conversation at a time, grounded in empathy and respect.
But the challenges? They were huge. Amy saw poverty and heartbreak on a scale she’d never encountered. She met women and children trapped in cycles of exploitation and abuse—some so silenced by fear and tradition that their stories might have gone untold. There were moments when the injustice was just overwhelming, and she questioned whether she could really make a difference.
One day, that struggle became heartbreakingly real. A young girl showed up at Amy’s doorstep, terrified and desperate. She’d escaped a temple where she’d been forced into ritual servitude—a practice that was quietly accepted and deeply hidden. Amy faced a choice: keep herself safe by turning the girl away, or take her in and risk angering powerful people.
Amy chose compassion. She welcomed the girl into her home, offering safety, comfort, and—maybe for the first time—a sense of belonging. Word began to spread, and soon, other children found their way to Amy’s door, each carrying their own story of pain and survival. Her small home quickly transformed into a sanctuary—a place where the most vulnerable could find hope and start to heal.
Of course, this work came at a price. Amy faced opposition from those who profited from the exploitation, and even from some within her own community who questioned her choices. There were threats, legal headaches, and days filled with deep discouragement. But through it all, she held on, convinced that every single life was precious and worth fighting for.
Life in India tested Amy’s faith and resilience every day. Illness, exhaustion, and loneliness showed up as constant companions. There were times when the needs seemed endless and her resources far too small. Yet, in the middle of all those struggles, Amy discovered a deeper sense of purpose. Pouring her life out in service, she realized, was never wasted.
Over time, that tiny sanctuary grew into a vibrant community. Children who had once known only fear and rejection found love, education, and a future. The work expanded, drawing in others who shared Amy’s vision for compassion and justice. What started as a single act of kindness slowly became a movement—one that touched countless lives.
Looking back, it’s easy to see what made the difference. Amy’s willingness to embrace a new world—to adapt, to listen, to serve—was at the heart of her impact. She understood something powerful: true leadership isn’t about power or being recognized. It’s about humility, sacrifice, and the courage to do what’s right—even when no one else is watching.

Chapter 4: Building a Sanctuary—The Birth and Growth of Dohnavur
Imagine the heart of southern India, where a simple act of protecting a frightened child slowly blossoms into something extraordinary. That’s how Dohnavur began—a place where the most vulnerable could finally feel safe, valued, and loved. Think about that: from one rescue, a whole community was born, all because Amy Carmichael refused to turn away from those in need.
The early days at Dohnavur? They were anything but easy. Resources were thin, and every day brought new challenges. Amy and her small team faced legal threats from people who just didn’t want them there. Health crises swept through the community. And then there was the daily struggle—just trying to feed, clothe, and educate a growing number of children. Some days, the obstacles towered so high, it must’ve felt almost impossible to keep going.
But here’s what’s incredible: even in those toughest moments, something beautiful was happening. The children who came to Dohnavur—most of them scared and unsure—slowly began to heal. Patient care, gentle discipline, and a steady circle of adults who truly cared made all the difference. Little by little, trust grew. Laughter returned. And hope started to replace fear. The home became a place of learning and joy—a world apart from the pain they’d left behind.
Amy led in her own unique way. She wasn’t interested in strict hierarchies or titles. Instead, she lived right alongside the children and her fellow workers. Simplicity, humility, and a sense of shared mission guided everything. Decisions were made together, and everyone pitched in, using their own strengths.
That sense of community? It shaped every part of life at Dohnavur. No one was seen as a charity case. Every child was welcomed as family, given real responsibilities, encouraged to learn, and taught to care for others. The goal wasn’t just to rescue—it was to restore. To help each child discover their own worth and their potential for the future.
Over time, Dohnavur caught the world’s attention. Visitors came from near and far, curious about the stories of transformation they’d heard. Some arrived skeptically, expecting just another orphanage. But what they found was a living, thriving community—built on love, respect, and deep faith.
And the impact? It reached far beyond the walls of Dohnavur. Many of the children who grew up there went out into the world, serving others and carrying forward what they’d learned. The work inspired new initiatives, challenged old ways of thinking, and proved that compassion really can create lasting change.
Of course, the journey wasn’t without heartache. Amy and her team faced plenty of criticism from people who misunderstood what they were doing or felt threatened by their boldness. There were betrayals, disappointments, and long seasons of loneliness. Amy herself battled health problems that sometimes kept her bedridden, unable to be right there in the thick of things.
But in those moments of weakness, Amy found something deeper. She realized that true strength isn’t about doing it all on your own. It’s about relying on God, leaning on others, and trusting that every small act of love makes a difference. That’s the lasting legacy of Dohnavur—not just the lives saved, but the powerful example set: a life poured out in service, marked by humility, perseverance, and hope that never gives up.

Chapter 5: Enduring Hardship—Suffering, Faith, and the Power of Small Acts.
As the years rolled on at Dohnavur, the mission kept growing, but so did the challenges. Amy’s health, which had always been a bit fragile, started to really decline. After a serious injury, she found herself mostly confined to her room—no longer able to jump into the daily routines she once led. For someone who’d always been right in the thick of things, this was a tough pill to swallow.
But here’s what’s incredible—Amy didn’t let her suffering or limitations define her. Instead, she chose to focus on what she could still do. From her small room, she wrote heartfelt letters, gave wise counsel, and prayed for those she cared about. The children and staff kept coming to her, drawn not just by her wisdom, but by that quiet strength she carried, even when she was at her weakest.
What really became clear was that Amy’s influence had never depended on her physical abilities. The lessons she’d shared—about being faithful in the little things, and the way love can heal and transform—kept on shaping the whole community. The work continued, held together by the values she’d planted and the example she’d set.
Think about it—most people, when they’re suffering, want to pull away or just give up. But Amy’s response was so different. She saw her pain as a chance to draw closer to God, to deepen her empathy, and to show others what perseverance really looks like. Her willingness to lean into her weakness, to accept help, and to trust in something bigger than herself became a quiet inspiration for everyone around her.
The real impact of Amy’s life wasn’t measured by big achievements or public recognition. Most of what she did was hidden—never noticed by the world. Still, it was those small, daily acts of faithfulness that built her legacy. The children who grew up at Dohnavur, the staff who kept the mission alive, and all the others touched by her example—each of them carried a piece of that legacy forward.
Looking back, you can see how Amy’s story turns the usual ideas of greatness upside down. She showed that true greatness isn’t about self-promotion or chasing after personal ambition—it’s about humility, sacrifice, and the quiet courage to do what’s right, even when no one’s watching.
Her life is a powerful reminder: faith, compassion, and even the smallest acts of love can change the world. And maybe, that’s the real measure of a life well lived.

Chapter 6: The Quiet Years—Leadership from the Shadows.
There’s a moment in every journey when things just... slow down. The world outside gets quieter, and the noise fades away. For Amy, those later years at Dohnavur brought a stillness she’d never really known before. You might think being mostly bedridden after her injury would have ended her influence. But for Amy, it was actually the start of something new—a fresh way to lead, to love, and to serve, even from the sidelines.
Imagine her in that small, sunlit room, watching the life of the community go by. She could hear children laughing in the courtyard, workers chatting softly as they took care of their daily chores, and somewhere in the distance, the gentle hum of prayer and song. Sure, her body was weaker, but Amy’s mind? Still sharp as ever. And her heart? Every bit as engaged.
Instead of walking the grounds, Amy wrote letters—hundreds of them. Each one was filled with encouragement, advice, and sometimes a gentle nudge in the right direction. Her words kept their warmth and conviction, just like when she was able to be everywhere at once.
There was this young woman, new to Dohnavur, who really struggled with the weight of responsibility. She constantly worried she’d never live up to Amy’s example. Then, one afternoon, she found a simple note slipped under her door: “You are not called to be Amy. You are called to be yourself, faithful in the small things.” Simple, right? But those words lifted a huge burden. It’s amazing, isn’t it, how a few honest words can completely change someone’s outlook?
Amy’s leadership during these years was almost invisible—quiet, in the background. She listened more than she spoke, trusted others to make decisions, and let go of controlling every little detail. That’s when it became clear: true influence isn’t about being at the center. It’s about empowering others to grow. The community learned to lean on each other, share the tough stuff, and celebrate even the smallest victories.
Of course, there were tough times too. Illness swept through the home more than once, and resources were stretched pretty thin. But the spirit of Dohnavur held strong, shaped by the values Amy had woven into every corner—humility, compassion, and that fierce commitment to caring for the vulnerable. Even as her own strength faded, Amy’s vision shone brighter than ever.
Looking back, those quiet years weren’t a decline at all. They were a time for deepening. Amy discovered that love doesn’t depend on staying busy or racking up achievements. It’s found in showing up, in praying, and in letting others take the spotlight. The seeds she’d planted so long ago kept growing, quietly and steadily, in the lives of everyone she touched.

Chapter 7: Writing for the World—Words as Legacy
You know, when the body grows weak, sometimes the mind finds surprising new ways to reach out. For Amy, writing wasn’t just a pastime—it became her lifeline, and even more, her legacy. Picture her, confined to her room, yet pouring her heart into books, poems, and letters. Every piece she wrote became a window into her soul... and a gift for people she might never meet face to face.
The stories Amy shared weren’t grand adventures or dramatic rescues. Instead, they were woven from the everyday fabric of life at Dohnavur—a child’s first real smile after months of silence, or a worker’s simple act of kindness. She even wrote about the slow, steady healing of wounds, both the ones you can see and the ones you can’t.
Amy’s honesty stood out. She never shied away from pain or struggle, but she always left room for hope, gently pointing to the possibility of redemption, even on the hardest days.
One evening, a staff member sat beside Amy’s bed, reading out a letter from a supporter in England. The letter was full of questions—about faith, suffering, and what sacrifice really means. Amy listened quietly, then dictated her reply: “We’re not asked to understand, only to trust. The path is hard, but the One who leads us is faithful.” That reply was shared with others, and—just like that—it became a source of comfort when times were tough.
Amy’s books didn’t just stay within Dohnavur’s walls. They traveled far, reaching missionaries, pastors, and everyday people searching for meaning. Her reflections on prayer, suffering, and what it costs to truly follow touched readers across cultures and generations. People found a kind of companionship in her words—a gentle reminder they weren’t alone in their struggles.
And here’s something to pay attention to: Amy’s greatest gift wasn’t rescuing or leading. It was her courage to be honest about the journey. She wrote about doubt and disappointment, those moments when faith feels almost impossible. But she also shared stories of grace, of quiet miracles that come when we choose to love, even when we’re afraid.
Through her writing, Amy’s influence grew, even as her world became smaller. She became a mentor to countless people she’d never meet—a comforting voice in a world that’s always hungry for hope.
So here’s the key takeaway: Amy’s words have become a lasting legacy, proof of how vulnerability and faith can reach far beyond our own limitations. Her story reminds us that sometimes, the most powerful thing we can do is simply share our truth.

Chapter 8: The Dohnavur Family—Generations of Change.
Over the years, the children who’d once arrived at Dohnavur, scared and alone, began to grow up. Some stayed, choosing to help carry on the work—they became teachers, nurses, and leaders in their own right. Others moved out into the world, but wherever they went, they took with them the lessons they’d learned in the safe haven Amy created.
One story stands out. There was a young man who’d first come to Dohnavur as a child, his past shadowed by loss and betrayal. But under Amy’s care, he found something he’d never had before—a true sense of belonging. Years later, he returned, this time with a family of his own. He knelt beside Amy’s chair, tears streaming down his face, and whispered, “You gave me a home. Now I want to give that gift to others.”
That moment said it all. The real impact of Amy’s work wasn’t measured by the number of children rescued, but by the lives that were changed forever.
Over time, the Dohnavur community really did become a family in every sense of the word. They celebrated weddings, welcomed new babies, grieved losses, and tackled all kinds of challenges together. The bonds they formed through hardship turned out to be even stronger than any blood tie. People who’d once felt like outsiders—orphans, widows, the poor—finally found a place where they truly belonged.
Amy was determined that the children would be educated—not just in academics, but in growing strong character. She taught them to serve, to forgive, and to stand up for what’s right. These values didn’t just shape individuals; they transformed the entire community. Dohnavur became a model for others who wanted to help the vulnerable.
Visitors kept coming, drawn in by stories of hope and transformation. Some arrived with doubts, expecting to see just another institution. Instead, they stepped into a living, breathing family—one filled with laughter, resilience, and a powerful sense of purpose. Many left changed themselves, inspired to bring a bit of Dohnavur’s spirit back to their own communities.
When we look back, it’s clear: Amy’s greatest legacy wasn’t a building or an organization. It was a way of life. She proved that when love is lived out in community, it can heal even the deepest wounds. The family she built keeps growing, still today—a living testament to the enduring power of compassion.

Let’s talk about something that takes real courage—facing the end, and the idea of letting go.
Chapter 9: Facing the End—Legacy and Letting Go.
There’s a special kind of bravery in meeting the final chapter of a journey. For Amy, those last years became a time of deep reflection and gentle release. She knew her days were drawing to a close, but she met that reality with the same honesty and faith that had always guided her.
Friends and neighbors often gathered in her room, filling it with stories, laughter, and songs. People came, not just to comfort Amy, but to share in the warmth she’d always offered. Sometimes she’d share a bit of wisdom, sometimes she’d just hold someone’s hand in complete, peaceful silence. And as the days passed, her focus shifted. She spoke less about her own journey, and more about the work that still needed to be done.
“This isn’t my legacy,” she’d remind everyone. “It belongs to all of us.”
In those final days, there was a deep sense of peace—a quiet assurance that the seeds she’d planted would keep growing, even after she was gone. Amy urged her community to look beyond her, to trust their own gifts, and to lean on the same faith that had carried them this far. She let go of control and trusted that the work would carry on.
One evening, as the sun dipped behind the fields, a group of children gathered outside her window. Their voices rose in a simple song of gratitude. Amy listened, eyes bright with tears—tears not of regret, but of deep fulfillment. In that moment, it was clear: her life hadn’t been wasted. Every act of love, every sacrifice, had blossomed in ways she could never have imagined.
When Amy passed, the sadness ran deep. But so did the gratitude. The community mourned, yes, but they also celebrated her—a woman whose life overflowed with service, humility, courage, and hope. Her memory wasn’t something heavy they carried—it became a light, a source of inspiration for everyone she’d touched.
Looking back, it’s easy to see Amy’s true gift. It wasn’t just in what she achieved, but in who she became. She showed all of us that a life poured out in love is never wasted. Even the smallest kindness can ripple out, shaping a community, changing the world. Her legacy isn’t in statues or plaques—it lives on in the people she loved, and in the community she helped build.

Chapter 10: The Ripple Effect — Amy’s Influence Across Generations
Even after Amy was gone, her story kept reaching farther and farther, touching lives well beyond Dohnavur. It’s like her example sent out waves—quiet at first, but powerful—urging people everywhere to step up for the vulnerable, to serve with humility, and to believe, deep down, that love really can break through any barrier.
Picture this: there’s a young woman in another country, feeling lost and unsure where she fits in. One day, she picks up a book by Amy and, flipping through its pages, discovers a sense of purpose she’s never felt before. She’s so moved, she writes to Dohnavur, asking if there’s any way she can help. Eventually, she makes the journey there herself, and her life—and the lives she touches—are changed forever.
All around the world, churches, schools, and organizations found themselves inspired by Amy’s story. Many of them started to weave her principles—simplicity, community, and sacrificial love—into the fabric of their own missions. And here’s the remarkable part: even people who never knew her name were still shaped by her legacy, as those values quietly spread from one person to the next.
The Dohnavur Fellowship, too, kept moving forward. They faced all kinds of new challenges—political storms, economic troubles, even the changes that come with shifting cultures. But through it all, the heart of Amy’s vision stayed strong: a promise to serve those with the least, to welcome anyone who needed a home, and to love—no matter what.
When you look back, it’s obvious that Amy’s influence isn’t something you can measure with numbers or charts. You find it in the small, quiet acts of kindness. In the lives rebuilt, the communities transformed bit by bit. Her life is proof that a single person, living with courage and compassion, can send ripples of hope across generations.

As we wrap up, let’s take a moment to really soak in what Amy Carmichael’s life means for you and me.
Her story isn’t just about the past—it’s an open invitation. Amy showed us that even in a world that can feel overwhelming, our small, faithful acts of love can truly make a difference.
Think about it: you don’t need a spotlight or a title to lead. Real leadership is found in humility, in showing up for others, in quiet acts of service that might never be recognized, but mean everything to someone.
Amy’s journey reminds us that even when we’re facing setbacks, loneliness, or pain, those hard moments can shape us, deepen our empathy, and give us the strength to keep going. Community grows when we share our burdens, our laughter, and our honest presence with one another.
And here’s the heart of it—legacy isn’t about how much we achieve, but about the lives we touch and help change along the way.
Maybe you’ve wondered if what you do really matters. If so, just remember Amy’s restless heart and her willingness to serve, even when she started with nothing. She faced all kinds of obstacles, but she never lost sight of the value in loving just one person at a time.
Her life proves that you don’t have to be extraordinary to make an extraordinary impact. It’s about having the courage to step into the needs around you, to give without keeping score, and to trust that your kindness—no matter how small—can start ripples of change.
So here’s what this means for you: don’t wait for perfect conditions or applause. Start right where you are, with what you have. Offer your presence, your compassion, and your willingness to serve and listen. That’s how you join this long line of ordinary people who, like Amy, discovered that a life poured out in love is never wasted.
The world’s waiting for your small, faithful acts. Take that first step—go and begin.
